# Did most of the schematic stuff
I'm aware wednesday is a _bit_ late to start your project but whatever. Today i chose some components and almost finished everything necessary for the schematic.

first i decided on my parts (which im still not 100% sure about)  for like 50 minutes

then i worked on the symbol schematic for the board im using. I'm using this one (the lilygo T7-S3, if you were wondering) because I had it lying around at home (it is pretty good), so i dont have to spend nearly half my budget on the board.

![entry1pic4](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/a5e16793e4a41e3703ae865c9968fcbba6f046967601eafafe9df76f5264009b.png)
_this took so loooooooong (prob like 25-ish min but it felt like longer...)_

40 PINS and im probably not even going to use more than like 7

anyways, instead, i get to spend half my budget on the distance sensor! Yay! we love expensive components!

![entry1pic6](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/62a6bafcc6ffb546da39260be19d1b8a4fa62d6e9871c007ec33935e341cda80.png)

i'm still not 100% sure ill use this, but it seems like the best one cuz the ultrasound ones have a FOV that's too wide, and this is one of the cheaper ones that isnt ultrasound

i then worked on the  symbol for it, which took me like 15 min of looking at the datasheet

![entry1pic2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/96bcbe4721178038239171516f6152b6310f8602e7541cdd2f4a63c5870c23ed.png)

i then realised that this was an I2C only thingy (thankfully before i started the schematic). i looked for my chip's i2C pins...

but i couldnt find them (i dont think it has any). The chip did however, advertise "a STEMMA QT / Qwiic JST-SH connector for easy I2C expansion," , meaning that it was compatible with I2C. after a little digging, i found out that i (might) need one of these connectors:

![entry1pic3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/04712aa221a244fb2fce67d12cd6a19ef61751a2cf2a2aaa1a9f6860b30a35c7.png)
_add it to the list_

this is a little weird because this is one of those things meant for prototyping (i think) so its a little weird to be using this with a pcb but _i cant find any I2C pins_

after this i started on the schematic and, since this was a pretty simple one, i finished it (almost) pretty easily
